root_cause.text: The `get_upper_ifindexes()` function in `kernel/bpf/devmap.c` lacks bounds checking when writing upper device interface indices into a stack-allocated array, allowing the number of upper devices (which can exceed the assumed `MAX_NEST_DEV` limit) to trigger a stack-out-of-bounds write.
root_cause.evidence: The patch diff shows that `get_upper_ifindexes()` was modified to accept a `max` parameter and check `if (n >= max)` before writing to `indexes[n++]`, and the callers `dev_map_enqueue_multi` and `dev_map_redirect_multi` pass `ARRAY_SIZE(excluded_devices) - 1` as the limit to prevent writing beyond the stack-allocated `excluded_devices` array.

intent_record.intent_summary: Add a boundary check to get_upper_ifindexes to prevent buffer overflow when retrieving upper device indexes.
intent_record.what: The function signature of `get_upper_ifindexes` is modified to accept a `max` parameter, and a boundary check is added inside the loop to return `-EOVERFLOW` if the number of processed upper devices exceeds this limit.
intent_record.how: This change prevents potential out-of-bounds memory writes to the `indexes` array by ensuring the loop terminates and returns an error if there are more upper devices than the allocated buffer size.
